question: A 48-year-old woman comes to the physician because of an increasingly painful swelling behind her right knee for the past 2 months. During this time, she has also had intermittent low-grade fever and she has been more fatigued than usual. She has not had any trauma to the knee. Over the past year, she has had occasional pain in her hands and wrists bilaterally. She has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She drinks 1–2 glasses of wine daily and occasionally more on weekends. Current medications include enalapril, metformin, and glimepiride. Her mother and older brother have osteoarthritis. She is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 68 kg (150 lb); BMI is 25 kg/m2. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 3-cm nontender mass in the right popliteal fossa that becomes prominent when the knee is extended. There is mild swelling and redness of her right knee joint. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "48-year-old woman with knee swelling" -> "painful swelling behind right knee" -> "nontender mass in right popliteal fossa" -> "mass prominent when knee extended" -> "intermittent low-grade fever" -> "fatigue" -> "occasional pain in hands and wrists" -> "possible inflammatory condition" -> "consider rheumatoid arthritis" -> 85%

CHAIN: "48-year-old woman with knee swelling" -> "3-cm nontender mass in right popliteal fossa" -> "mass suggests possible cyst or vascular issue" -> "mild swelling and redness of right knee joint" -> "intermittent low-grade fever" -> "fatigue" -> "consider systemic inflammatory disease" -> "possible rheumatoid arthritis" -> 80%

CHAIN: "48-year-old woman with knee swelling" -> "painful swelling behind right knee" -> "nontender mass in right popliteal fossa" -> "mass prominent when knee extended" -> "intermittent low-grade fever" -> "fatigue" -> "family history of osteoarthritis" -> "age and symptoms suggest degenerative disease" -> "consider osteoarthritis" -> 70%

CHAIN: "48-year-old woman with knee swelling" -> "3-cm nontender mass in right popliteal fossa" -> "mass suggests possible cyst" -> "mild swelling and redness of right knee joint" -> "intermittent low-grade fever" -> "fatigue" -> "consider systemic lupus erythematosus" -> "less likely due to lack of other systemic symptoms" -> 60%

CHAIN: "48-year-old woman with knee swelling" -> "painful swelling behind right knee" -> "nontender mass in right popliteal fossa" -> "mass prominent when knee extended" -> "intermittent low-grade fever" -> "fatigue" -> "occasional pain in hands and wrists" -> "consider psoriatic arthritis" -> "less likely due to lack of skin symptoms" -> 55%
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including the painful swelling behind the knee, intermittent low-grade fever, fatigue, and bilateral hand and wrist pain, suggest an inflammatory process. The presence of a nontender mass in the popliteal fossa that becomes prominent with knee extension is characteristic of a Baker's cyst, which is often associated with underlying joint conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis. Given her age, gender, and symptoms, rheumatoid arthritis is the most likely diagnosis, especially considering the family history of osteoarthritis and her own joint symptoms.
